bounds.publication: Two read requests, FIFO worker/main continuations, epochs 0 through 3, two opaque permission scopes, foreground, lock and closure. Changes that exceed the epoch bound are excluded.
bounds.selection: Two admitted native reviews over at most two of three symbolic items, one input-selection replacement, revisions 0 and 1, expiration, closure and one FIFO worker. Each request is copied and dispatched at most once.
bounds.premises: The bridge settles each read once and invokes a successful publication callback after delivery. Native activity results belong to the admitted pending request. Catalog mutations atomically validate the captured item revision and return their verified outcome.
bounds.conformance: The maintained node suite compiles exact Java ticket/submit/publication methods, request copying/admission prefix, constructor result callback, resume continuation and apply/close methods into a JVM fixture. Controlled platform ports verify 13 publication and 9 selection scenarios. The existing exact permanent-deletion JVM check also runs.
bounds.limits: This is source-level JVM scenario conformance. Android lifecycle and permission delivery, MediaStore, ContentResolver, Looper threads and physical devices remain external. No tracked production host registration/call site was found outside the module's consumer fixture. Multiple volumes, query-fence deadlines, real media bytes, Replace continuations, unbounded epochs and process recovery remain separate.

assumptions: Weak fairness of the FIFO worker beginning an admitted read, the active I/O callback returning success or failure, and main-thread publication. This assumes callback settlement and scheduling, without requiring I/O success.
No fairness. A queued worker, active read or posted main callback can remain stalled indefinitely.

Weak fairness of native approval or rejection, an accepted waiting request observing resume or closed-activity destruction, its synchronous captured resume continuation, and finite worker/response callbacks. This assumes a native decision and lifecycle settlement. It requires neither approval nor successful writes.
No fairness. An owner decision, lifecycle event or worker callback can remain absent.
